name: push-tag-release-agent-carve-out
body:
Law (prose; assessed by review): the **"push/tag are human-approved acts"** rule binds every agent and every path EXCEPT the deliberately-invoked `release-agent`: that generated per-repo agent is the ONLY agent granted `git push *` and `git tag *`, and its grant is `ask` — every push/tag command prompts for explicit human approval. It may run `scripts/release.sh` and then push/tag itself. Because the grant is confined to one deliberately-invoked agent and each op prompts, the human gate surfaces twice: the EXPLICIT USER CONSENT the `codebase-navigator` must obtain before dispatching it via the `subagent` tool, and the per-command `ask`. Every OTHER generated agent — the core/root `implementer`, each per-subsystem `<name>-implementer`, and each tiered `test-implementer` — gets NO push/tag grant at all (absent verbs are denied by deny-by-default).

The carve-out is an AGENT-policy statement only: the `apg` binary never pushes or tags — it is git2-only (`default-features = false`; the git CLI is never shelled out to) — and `scripts/release.sh` never pushes. The binary-doc surfaces (`Cargo.toml`, `src/git/mod.rs`, `src/project_cmd/mod.rs` and the two git e2e tests) describe push/tag as human-approved acts. Broadening the release-agent's grant from `ask` to `allow`, granting push/tag to any other generated agent, or weakening the navigator's consent gate violates this law. The law is restated by `requirements.requirement.push-tag-human-approved-release-only`. Satisfaction is assessed by review.
